proof.text: Throughout, $D^b_c$ has the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. It is closed under shifts, finite direct sums, retracts and distinguished triangles: in the long exact cohomology sequence, each cohomology is an extension of a kernel by a cokernel; these are constructible by [thm-constructible-serre]. Finitely many bounded intervals have a common finite bound. Right-derived direct image is triangulated by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. The triangles of [lem-sf-derived-truncation-triangle], applied successively to a bounded interval of cohomology, therefore reduce assertions about bounded constructible input complexes to their cohomology sheaves, without requiring a bound uniform in the sheaf. For later use, a finite map has exact direct image on abelian sheaves by [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact]. The comparison [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison] implies vanishing of its higher module direct images too. Its degree-zero direct image preserves constructibility by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-fp-pushforward-constructible]; here finite maps between Noetherian schemes are finitely presented by [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth]. Thus finite direct image preserves $D^b_c$.

source.place: XIII 1.1.2 and 3.7.2; finite map facts: Stacks Tags 03QP and 0GJ2

proof.text: For each $c\geq0$, prove simultaneously for all Noetherian quasi-excellent $X$ with $\ell$ invertible, all open immersions $j:V\hookrightarrow X$ and all $K\in D^b_c(V,B)$ the assertion $P_c$: there is a closed $C\subseteq X$ with every point of height $>c$ such that $Rj_*K$ is bounded constructible on $X\setminus C$. Height means $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Noetherian and quasi-excellent hypotheses persist under finite-type maps, closed subschemes and open restrictions by [lem-per-quasi-excellent-finite-type-stability]. Derived restriction to a target open or etale object commutes with direct image, with its adjunction maps, by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-slice-localization]. For $c=0$, take $C=\overline V\setminus V$: it contains no generic point of an irreducible component of $X$, and hence all its points have positive height. On $V$, the direct image restricts to $K$; on $X\setminus\overline V$ it is zero. These two disjoint opens are $X\setminus C$, proving $P_0$. Fix $c\geq1$ and assume $P_{c-1}$ for all these schemes and complexes, not just the current pair.

source.place: XIII 3.1.1 and 3.1.4 (with the same argument for a nondense open)

proof.text: First establish the constant-input case of $P_c$ for an integral $X$ and a nonempty (hence dense) open $j:V\hookrightarrow X$. By $P_{c-1}$ choose a bad closed set $C$ whose points have height at least $c$. It has finitely many irreducible components. Components of height $>c$ can be left in the new bad set. It suffices to prove bounded constructibility near the generic point $t$ of each height-$c$ component $T$: remove the other components temporarily so that $Rj_*B_V$ is good on $X\setminus T$. Once such neighbourhoods are found, their union with $X\setminus C$ is an open good locus; its closed complement contains no point of height $\leq c$. Indeed any strict specialization of a height-$c$ generic point has height at least $c+1$, by appending one prime to a chain. All changes here are open restrictions, justified by Step 2.

source.place: XIII 3.2.2 (finite set of generic bad points)

proof.text:
Choose the diagram $W_i\xrightarrow{a_i}E_i\xrightarrow{e_i}X'\xrightarrow p X$ and $W_i\to Y=\coprod_bY_b$ of [lem-per-prime-to-ell-uniformization-standard-form], for $(X,V)$. Apply [lem-per-birational-bad-locus-comparison] to $K=B_V$ and to $P_{c-1}$. Its hypotheses are exactly the integral pair, the proper birational $p$, the completely decomposed etale family, and the bad component of height $c$ isolated in Step 3. After shrinking around $t$ it supplies $T'=\coprod_\alpha T'_\alpha$ finite over $T$, the sections $s_\alpha:T'_\alpha\to E_{i_\alpha}$, and a map
$$A=(Rj_*B_V)|_T\longrightarrow C_1=(p_T)_*((Rj'_*B_{V'})|_{T'})$$
whose cone is bounded constructible. All schemes in the diagram are Noetherian and quasi-excellent by the stability cited in Step 2. It remains to show $C_1\in D^b_c(T,B)$.

Fix $\alpha$ and abbreviate $E=E_{i_\alpha}$, $a:W=W_{i_\alpha}\to E$, $r=r_{i_\alpha}$, and $S=T'_\alpha$. Let $V_E,V_W$ be the inverse images of $V$, with open inclusions $j_E,j_W$. The trace of [lem-pur-quasifinite-flat-weighted-trace] for $a|_{V_E}$ has composite $B_{V_E}\to a_*B_{V_W}\to B_{V_E}$ equal to multiplication by $r$. Since $\ell\nmid r$, multiply the trace by $r^{-1}\in B$ to split the unit. Apply $Rj_{E*}$ and use [lem-cbc-etale-derived-direct-image-coherence] and finite exactness from Step 1: this makes $Rj_{E*}B_{V_E}$ a retract of $a_*Rj_{W*}B_{V_W}$. Pull back along $s_\alpha:S\to E$. Proper base change for the finite $a$ is [det-properbasechange-modules], giving
$$s_\alpha^*a_*Rj_{W*}B_{V_W}\simeq(a_S)_*((Rj_{W*}B_{V_W})|_{W\times_E S}).$$
Here all coefficients are killed by $\ell$, so the torsion hypothesis is satisfied. Etale slice localization from Step 2 identifies $s_\alpha^*Rj_{E*}B_{V_E}$ with $(Rj'_*B_{V'})|_S$ because $e_{i_\alpha}s_\alpha:S\to X'$ is the inclusion. Thus this last complex is a retract of the displayed finite direct image.

Write $g:A\to C_1$ for Step 4 and let $C_3$ be the finite sum over $\alpha$ of the complexes in Step 5 pushed to $T$. That step supplies $u:C_1\to C_3$ and a normalized trace $v:C_3\to C_1$ with $vu=1$. Put $S'''_\alpha=W_{i_\alpha}\times_{E_{i_\alpha}}T'_\alpha$ and $b_\alpha:S'''_\alpha\to T$; these maps are finite. Let $h_\alpha:S'''_\alpha\to Y$ be the given maps. By [lem-per-regular-normal-crossings-constant-image], $Rj_{Y*}B_{V_Y}\in D^b_c(Y,B)$, so
$$D=\bigoplus_\alpha(b_\alpha)_*h_\alpha^*Rj_{Y*}B_{V_Y}\in D^b_c(T,B).$$
Pullback is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], so commutes with cohomology and preserves its bounds. Pulling back a finite stratification and its finite locally constant restrictions preserves constructibility by [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-set-pullback], applied to the underlying abelian sheaves; finite direct image preserves it by Step 1. The canonical base-change units give maps $d:A\to D$ and $w:D\to C_3$. The two chains $W_i\to E_i\to X'\to X$ and $W_i\to Y\to X$ have the same composite. The composition formula of [lem-fin-module-exchange-composite-base-change], applied to the open $j$ along these two chains and then restricted to $S'''_\alpha$, therefore gives the explicit equality $wd=ug$. It uses no invertibility of base change along $W_i\to Y$. Consequently $g=vug=vwd$ factors through $D$.

Apply [lem-per-thick-verdier-quotient-kernel] to $D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ and its thick subcategory $D^b_c(T,B)$, whose closure properties were proved in Step 1. The cone of $g:A\to C_1$ is in this subcategory, so $Q(g)$ is an isomorphism. Step 6 factors $g$ through $D\in D^b_c$, so $Q(g)=0$. An invertible zero map has zero source: its inverse composed with it is the identity and is zero. Thus $Q(A)=0$, and the kernel criterion gives $A\in D^b_c(T,B)$. If $T'$ is empty, Step 4 already has zero target and the same argument applies. Together with bounded constructibility off $T$, this proves it on the neighbourhood of $t$: combine the two finite stratifications, one on $T$ and one on its open complement, and take the maximum of their bounds. Step 3 now proves $P_c$ for constant input on every integral $X$.

It remains to prove $P_c$ for all input sheaves and all $X$. For fixed $j:V\hookrightarrow X$, the class of constructible sheaves satisfying it is stable under finite sums, extensions and retracts: take a finite union of their bad closed sets, and apply Step 1 on its complement. By [lem-per-constructible-finite-open-constant-generation], it is enough to treat $\pi_*k_!B_W$ with $\pi:V'\to V$ finite, $V'$ integral, and $k:W\hookrightarrow V'$ nonempty open. Apply [thm-pqf-zmt-factorization] to the separated quasi-finite finite-type map $V'\to X$, obtaining $V'\xrightarrow{j'}X'\xrightarrow{\bar\pi}X$ with $\bar\pi$ finite. Replace $X'$ by the reduced closure of $V'$; its intersection with the open $V'$ is unchanged because $V'$ is reduced, so $X'$ is integral and $V'$ is dense in it. It remains Noetherian quasi-excellent by Step 2. By [lem-cbc-etale-derived-direct-image-coherence] and finite exactness,
$$Rj_*\pi_*k_!B_W\simeq\bar\pi_*Rj'_*k_!B_W.$$
Thus we must first find the desired good locus for the rightmost open direct image on the integral scheme $X'$.

Let $i:H=V'\setminus W\hookrightarrow V'$ be the reduced closed complement. The sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] gives the triangle $k_!B_W\to B_{V'}\to i_*B_H\to$. By Step 7, $Rj'_*B_{V'}$ is good outside a closed subset of height $>c$ in $X'$. Put $\bar H=\overline H\subset X'$ with the reduced structure, let $m:H\hookrightarrow\bar H$ be open, and $n:\bar H\hookrightarrow X'$ be closed. Composition and finite exactness give
$$Rj'_*i_*B_H=n_*Rm_*B_H.$$
By $P_{c-1}$ on $\bar H$, the right side is good outside a closed subset $C_H\subseteq\bar H$ of height at least $c$ in $\bar H$. Since $X'$ is integral and $W$ is nonempty, $\bar H$ is a proper closed subset. A prime chain of length $c$ in $\bar H$ extends to one of length $c+1$ in $X'$ by placing the generic point of $X'$ before it. Thus $C_H$ has height $>c$ in $X'$. Outside the union of these two bad sets, the triangle and Step 1 show $Rj'_*k_!B_W\in D^b_c$. If $H$ is empty, its contribution is zero.

Let $C'\subseteq X'$ be the closed bad subset obtained in Step 9. Its image $C=\bar\pi(C')$ is closed because $\bar\pi$ is finite. For $x'\in C'$ and $x=\bar\pi(x')$, the local dimension inequality [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-inequality-quasi-finite] gives $\operatorname{ht}_{X'}(x')\leq\operatorname{ht}_X(x)$, since a finite ring map is quasi-finite at every prime. Consequently every point of $C$ has height $>c$. Over $X\setminus C$, the finite pushforward in Step 8 comes entirely from $X'\setminus C'$; it is bounded constructible by Step 1 and target-open localization in Step 2. This proves $P_c$ for each generator, hence for every constructible sheaf by Step 8. Successive truncation triangles from Step 1 prove it for every bounded constructible $K$. This completes the induction, with $X$ and $K$ varying at each rank.

Apply $P_c$ for every $c$ to the original pair $(j,M[0])$. Write $C_c$ for the resulting closed subsets and $O_c=T\setminus C_c$ for their good open complements. Each $x\in T$ has finite height by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-finite-krull-dimension] applied to $\mathcal O_{T,x}$. Taking $c\geq\operatorname{ht}_T(x)$ forces $x\notin C_c$, so $(O_c)$ covers $T$. Quasi-compactness gives a finite subcover. The finitely many cohomological bounds on those opens have a common maximum, so $R^qj_*M$ vanishes above that maximum. For each remaining degree combine finite constructible stratifications on a finite open subcover: successively remove earlier opens from each later one and intersect their strata; these differences and intersections are locally closed constructible subsets in the Noetherian space. This gives a finite stratification of $T$ with finite locally constant restrictions. Thus every $R^qj_*M$ is constructible. Right-derived direct image of a degree-zero sheaf has no negative cohomology; take $N_M\geq0$ at least the resulting upper bound. Empty $T$, empty $U$, and $M=0$ give the zero complex and $N_M=0$; $j=1_T$ also has this bound. The finite subcover depends on $M$, as allowed in the statement.

title: Gabber finiteness for a quasi-excellent open immersion on sheaves
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and $B$ a finite field of characteristic $\ell$. Let $T$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning a scheme with a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Assume that every affine open of $T$ has quasi-excellent coordinate ring [def-exc-excellent-ring] and that $\ell$ is a unit in every local ring of $T$. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. For every constructible sheaf $M$ of modules over the constant sheaf $B_U$ on the ordinary small etale site [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], all higher direct images $R^qj_*M$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] are constructible $B_T$-module sheaves, and there is an integer $N_M\geq0$ such that $R^qj_*M=0$ for $q>N_M$. The bound may depend on $M$; no assertion about arbitrary nonconstructible sheaves is made.
